title: Enterprise escalation: urgent throughput rescue after allocator VM-remap causing tokens/sec collapse
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
An enterprise customer running a heterogeneous mix of quantized and full-precision model variants reported a sudden tokens/sec collapse (~60% drop) across Hosted and Dedicated clusters after a regional maintenance window. The customer experienced severe user-facing latency increases for inference routes pinned to that region and opened an escalation at 2026-03-10 07:12 UTC.

Observed symptoms:
- Immediate tokens/sec drop from ~1200 to ~450 on affected worker pools for 30+ minutes post-maintenance.
- First-token throughput (FTT) increased by ~3.5x for affected requests; streaming start delayed.
- Regression reproduced in private clusters with similar allocator configuration.
- No application-level changes from customer; traffic profile unchanged.

Scope and blast radius:
- Hosted API region-eu-west-3 and a subset of Dedicated pools used by 3 enterprise customers. Private on-prem clusters with same allocator heuristics also saw smaller spikes.

Initial triage and hypothesis:
- Telemetry pointed to elevated page-faults and slow memory remap operations on worker VMs during the warmup phase after maintenance.
- Heap/allocator metrics show increased fragmentation and a fallback path in the in-house allocator triggered by VM remap order interactions with the kernel (seen in kernel vm_events).
- The allocator fallback increases lock contention and leads to delayed KV-cache priming and slower kernel selection for quantized kernels, manifesting as tokens/sec loss and FTT regressions.

Immediate mitigations deployed:
1) Rolled a runtime patch (hotfix candidate) to bypass the allocator fallback path for warmup-critical threads in the affected pools (canary in two Dedicated hosts) — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621
2) Enabled cross-region routing fallback for the affected customers to route new sessions to unaffected regions for low-latency routes (temporary traffic steering) — runbook step triggered.
3) Increased warmup concurrency and prefetch windows for bursting tenants as a stopgap to rebuild KV cache faster.

Root cause (confirmed after replay):
- During the maintenance, kernel memory remap order combined with our allocator's anti-fragmentation heuristic. The heuristic attempted aggressive compaction which triggered a heavy lock path that serialized warmup allocations. This serialization delayed KV cache priming and quantized kernel JIT/cache activation. The downstream effect was dramatically reduced token emission rates until compaction completed.

Fix plan and roll-forward:
- Short-term (hotfix): ship the bypass patch that avoids aggressive compaction for warmup threads and forces a fast-path allocation for kernel/JIT caches. Goal: restore tokens/sec to baseline without a full allocator overhaul. (Target: rollout to all affected Dedicated pools by 2026-03-14 22:00 UTC; Hosted region follow-up in rolling controlled deploy.)
- Mid-term: instrument allocator internals and add metrics (compaction frequency, compaction time, fallback-path-count) and add an automatic slow-path detector that stalls compaction if warmup traffic is present.
- Long-term: redesign compaction heuristic to be workload-aware (separate aggressive compaction windows for low-traffic windows and safe warmup fast-path.)

Testing and verification:
- Canary rollout observed tokens/sec recovery to within 5% of baseline on two Dedicated canaries after hotfix. Streaming FTT reduced to expected range.
- Synthetic replay harness used by QE to simulate warmup traffic verified mitigation across quantized and FP model variants.

Monitoring & alerting changes:
- Created a composite alert that fires on simultaneous: tokens/sec drop >40% + compaction_time > 200ms for >= 5min.
- Dashboard: added allocator compaction panel and VM remap event overlay for correlation dashboards (link below).

Documentation & customer comms:
- Sent interim incident update to customer at 2026-03-10 14:40 UTC explaining temporary routing and ongoing rollback.
- Drafted postmortem template and scheduled on-call rotation for follow-ups.

Artifacts and links:
- Runtime PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621
- Canary runbook: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Infra/pages/AlloHotfixCanary
- Customer dashboard slice: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/enterprise/esc-880999
- Replay harness job: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/replay/esc-880999

Next steps (owner: Rafael Ortiz):
- Complete staged rollout to remaining Dedicated pools and Hosted region (target 2026-03-14).
- Merge additional telemetry PR to add compaction metrics (ENG-PR-4727).
- Complete postmortem by 2026-03-18, include proposed mid-term allocator changes and schedule engineering work.
